title: You cant backtest a gamma level strategy further back than about six months, and the backtester isnt the problem
author: person-person12
selftext:
I went to test something simple. Price gets to the call wall, i fade it. Price loses the gamma flip, i get short. Thats the whole rule set.

I could not run it further back than May of this year, and once i worked out why, the reason turned out to be the more interesting part.

**A gamma level is not a price, its a snapshot of open interest by strike on a given day.** To know where the call wall sat on the 14th of March 2024 you need that whole chain as it stood that morning, strike by strike. Nobody is selling you it. Chains get overwritten as positions move, and the one public source i had been counting on retired its historical chains last month, so the paid route closed too.

What you can get going back years is the **single daily net number** for the S&P, published since 2011. Thats one figure a day for the whole index. Its genuinely useful and i use it, but "net gamma was negative that day" is a different rule from "price tapped the call wall at 24,150 and rejected". One is a regime filter, the other is a level, and only the first one has history.

So a wall or flip test in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) starts in May for me, because thats when the levels i hold start, and i would rather have six honest months than four years of numbers i reconstructed.

**\_\_\_\_\_**

Heres the part that actually bothers me. Ask most of these AI backtesting sites for a gamma flip strategy on five years of NQ and you will get an equity curve back. They are not finding chains that dont exist, they are **computing a level out of the price data they already have** and calling it the flip. It looks fine, it has a sharpe, and its a made up line.

Its like asking somebody what the traffic was like on a street in 2019 and getting a confident answer because they looked at how wide the road is.

**\_\_\_\_\_**

Three things worth asking of any options flow backtest, mine included

1) what is the **source** of the level on a date before your data provider existed

2) was the level used for a candle published **before** that candle opened, or stamped on after the fact

3) what happens on a gap, a holiday week, a missed refresh

Six months is a short sample and im not calling it an edge off that. Its still the only window where every level in the test was a level that existed on the day.

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body: Point 2 is the one I'd check first. I had a backtest once that used the close of a bar before the bar was finished, and most of the edge went away when I fixed it. A level stamped on after the fact is the same bug, just harder to spot.
